highlights.title: Canelo Álvarez v Christian Mbilli: WBC super-middleweight championship – live
highlights.summary: Álvarez challenges for Mbilli’s 168lb title in Riyadh. Mexican star fights for first time since Crawford loss. Reach out to Bryan on Bluesky or by email. Here come the fighters. First it’s Mbilli, entering first despite his status as the champion, wearing a black tee and red trunks.
body: No surprises here. Canelo Álvarez has won a 12-round decision over Christian Mbilli to capture the WBC super-middleweight title. The official scores were 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110. (The Guardian had it 117-110).

Mbilli surely needs a knockout to retain his title, yet the urgency is nowhere to be seen. Álvarez is practically inviting the champion to come forward, but the Frenchman remains oddly hesitant to engage. It’s a baffling finish from a fighter whose reputation was built on relentless pressure. Álvarez will be a three-time super-middleweight champion as soon as these scores are tallied...

More of the same. Álvarez in total control. Says Stephen “Breadman” Edwards, the respected Philadelphia-based boxing trainer: “Mbilli is lucky this is not the Canelo of 2018-21. He would’ve been stopped already. Mbilli is not performing well [in my opinion]. He’s outthinking himself.”

highlights.title: 5 Best Nintendo Switch Games That Desperately Need Switch 2 Upgrades, Ranked
highlights.summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 has been on one heck of run through launch. Though it has yet to see new installments of some heavy-hitter franchises, Nintendo’s latest console has built up an impressive library of games over its first year and a half.
body: Though Nintendo has upgraded a fair amount of the Switch’s crown jewels so far, there are still a few games begging for the Edition treatment. That includes some top-tier games that could benefit from a tech boost and more niche ones that feel built for the Switch 2’s mouse controls. If there are any more Switch 2 Editions left in the tank, we hope that these make the cut.

Following the release of the Switch 2’s excellent Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, a Three Houses boost feels like a no-brainer. The tactics game brought the series to new heights of popularity in 2019 and gave the Switch one of its finest RPGs. It could use a visual and performance boost to bring it more in line with Fortune’s Weave as a treat, but that’s not the main draw. It would be a great excuse to bundle in all the content featured in its Expansion Pass, including its Cindered Shadows DLC. Heck, toss in a few alternate Fortune’s Weave costumes for characters like Seteth who appear in both games as a bonus.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

highlights.title: ‘Green Room’ Director Remembers Patrick Stewart as a ‘F—ing Sweetheart’ and Credits Him for Rescuing the Film: He ‘Swooped Down’ ‘Into Our Cruddy Ass Movie and Saved Us’
highlights.summary: “Green Room” writer and director Jeremy Saulnier paid tribute to late actor Patrick Stewart, who starred in the film and whom he credits with saving the day when they were “close to shutting down,” during a 10th-anniversary screening of the 2015 film in Los Angeles on Friday.
body: Then, “Patrick Stewart, out of the blue, sort of expressed interest in the project,” said Saulnier. “And in a whirlwind about a week later, I was on the phone with him. I left the stage, ‘Maybe we’re gonna have to break down the sets and shut the whole movie down.’

He continued: “Instead, this dude came out of nowhere, from way above our sort of zone, and just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us, and said yes. And the movie was instantly greenlit; we moved forward. And I thank him for just taking that leap and making ‘Green Room’ a thing.”

Saulnier remembered the actor as a “fucking sweetheart, true gentleman, a kind leader to our whole cast,” and recounted his idea to add “a little something” to one scene: “I was like, ‘What is it, Patrick?’ He’s like, ‘Well, during this one part of the scene, when the camera’s coming through there, I’d like to say, “Fuck!” And I was like, ‘And?’ ‘Just fuck.’ Permission granted, sir,” Saulnier recounted. “And I just knew that he was completely aligned with the film, its aesthetic, its intentions and with me as a filmmaker, and it was just this lovely, lovely thing.”

highlights.title: Everybody’s macrodosing on microdramas
highlights.summary: Following the news that Margot Robbie’s turn on Neighbours is fated to be clipped into a microdrama, Ima Caldwell explains the ins and outs of the rapidly growing medium of social media soap operas, werewolves and all. 10 chaotic questions with Michael Theo: ‘I want to be on Dancing with the Stars!
body: Leading questions: ‘My sister-in-law is nearly 40 but cannot handle losing at board games. What can I do?’

Ima Caldwell: Television distilled, for your dopamine-fiending pleasure! A microdrama is usually an episodic series filmed (or reframed) in portrait orientation, for phone screens. Each instalment clocks in at around 60-90 seconds and they’re aired to social media and on specialised microdrama streaming apps. They’re generally packed with enough plot twists to make daytime television look like slow cinema. One producer described them as “soap operas on cocaine”. Maybe the sort of thing you’d end up watching drunk at 2am.

Alyx: I downloaded ReelShort the other day and was kind of shocked at the content. Forced marriage mafia plotlines; Secretly Pregnant by the Homeless Billionaire. It basically looked like the greatest hits (and misses) of Kindle Unlimited’s alpha male romance charts. Is the Neighbours microdrama going to be that hectic?

highlights.title: 10 Classic '90s RPGs That Have Aged Like Fine Wine, Ranked
highlights.summary: The 1990s proved a pivotal decade for gaming, fueled by technological advancements and new businesses that would go on to leave a lasting impact on the industry. The '90s saw the release of both the original Sony PlayStation (1995) and the Nintendo 64 (1996) which brought iconic titles such as…
body: New opportunities in the '90s also helped pave the way for RPGs, and although countless technological advancements have been made in the past three decades, many of those games are still worth playing today. The games are just that good — and several of them also helped provide the framework for modern titles.

Nearly a decade before Square Enix was formed, two of the gaming industry's biggest players — Squaresoft and Enix — joined forces in 1995 to create an RPG that remains highly regarded today. In Chrono Trigger, players control Crono and a band of adventurers who travel through time to stop a global catastrophee and save the world from the alien entity Lavos. The game combines some of the best elements of the genre: a captivating story, charming music, and fluid combat based on the Active Time Battle system used in early Final Fantasy titles.

Perhaps the most enduring quality of Chrono Trigger, even after 30 years, is its replayability. The game has more than a dozen endings to discover, including a special secret ending that pays tribute to the developers — endearingly called the "Dream Team" — who brought Chrono Trigger to life.

body: Whether it’s Pokémon Sleep turning towards nightmarish ghosts like Gengar, or a growing cast of horror characters in Fortnite, there’s a good chance one game or other will land a scare.

This year, Epic Games, Zynga, The Pokémon Company, Scopely, Intelligent Systems and even The New York Times are among those dressing up their games for the occasion. Many of them also recently landed among our Top 50 Mobile Game Makers of 2026.

The aptly named Fortnitemares event has brought a month of cursed content to Epic Games’ flagship, tapping into a lineup of characters like Freddy Krueger, Ghost Face and Freddy Fazbear. In fact, characters from the Five Nights at Freddy’s universe are going all-in on the fright factor, with their outfits able to show battle damage.

Other IPs trickling in throughout October have included Hollow Knight, Slender Man, Beetlejuice and Obsession. Meanwhile, gameplay has seen players firing pumpkin rockets, teleporting around and dropping into Reload’s Nitemare Island.

highlights.summary: "I still see him, but he is fine," the 'Basic Instinct' actor said of the three-time Oscar winner who has stayed out of the spotlight in recent years.
body: Michael Douglas is sharing a rare update on Jack Nicholson, who has largely remained out of the spotlight in recent years.
During an appearance to promote his memoir One Helluva Ride in Swansea, the Basic Instinct actor was asked about his relationship with Nicholson.
“I would have liked to have acted with Jack,” Douglas said, per The Independent. “He’s not working any more. He’s well. He has disappeared. I know that.”
Douglas is 82, and Nicholson is 89. The two actors only professionally collaborated on 1975’s One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest, which Douglas produced and Nicholson starred in.

highlights.title: Get in the spirit with these horrors from YouTube
highlights.summary: Rather than recommend a single horror film or an unsettling album for our final installment of spooky season recs, I present you with a small selection of creepy, disturbing, and just plain weird videos from YouTube. There's a little something for everyone here.
body: Close out the Halloween season with these creepy, weird, and unsettling videos from YouTube.

This 1983 short film from Cecelia Condit found its audience over 30 years later when it was uploaded to YouTube and eventually found its way to Reddit. If you’ve ever wondered what a feminist musical about cannibals directed by David Lynch would be like, wonder no more. Possibly in Michigan is only 12 minutes long, but it has inspired hours of YouTube videos dedicated to analyzing its deeply unsettling imagery and meaning.

The line between horror and comedy is razor thin, and Homemade Gatorade expertly threads that line. It’s bizarre, uncomfortable, and uncanny. It blends stiff animation with heavily processed video to create something quite unique. I’m never sure if I should be laughing or squirming in terror with every turn this road trip short takes.

highlights.title: Every Resident Evil Game, Ranked From Worst to Best
highlights.summary: After decades of misses, 2026 gave us one of the best gaming adaptations of all time. Well, sort of. Zach Cregger’s take on Resident Evil was a hit among critics who have praised the horror movie for its delightfully playful tone.
body: There are people out there who will argue that Resident Evil 5 is an underrated gem. They will say that there’s more nuance to its story than its lousy reputation would have you think. They will say that despite its problems, it really sings in co-op. To each their own, truly — but I would rather be mauled by zombie dogs than replay Resident Evil 5. If you’re an advocate for it, I implore you to revisit it to get an updated feel for a torturously clumsy third-person shooter that has aged like raw fish.

If I’m being honest, I’d consider myself a Resident Evil 6 apologist. I know that’s a ludicrous thing to say after slamming Resident Evil 5 supporters, but look: Resident Evil 6 actually gets the series’ tone. It takes the B-movie energy of the original games and takes them to the silliest peak possible. It plays terribly and features some storylines that are absolute duds, but Leon’s arc is an underappreciated bit of Resident Evil wackiness that deserves its flowers.
points: After decades of misses, 2026 gave us one of the best gaming adaptations of all time.

highlights.title: Frank Miller on Why He’s Relieved There Are Fewer Comic Book Adaptations Now: They Were ‘Really in Danger of Losing Their Souls’
highlights.summary: Comic book writer and screenwriter Frank Miller – whose work includes “300,” “Sin City” and “Batman: The Dark Knight Returns” – returned this week to Lucca Comics and Games, an event that spans the gamut of geek culture and pop entertainment.
body: Variety spoke to Miller about politics, art and why he’s relieved there are fewer comic book movies this year.

Would you agree that there has been a slight dip in the comic book to movie pipeline? I would hope so. Yeah, really. It had really gotten so out of control that comics had started losing much of their own identity. I have been arguing vehemently for comics to start asserting their own purpose again and asserting their own identity as a literary form.

Do you think there were too many comic book artists and writers aiming for movie and TV deals? Oh, without question. Just because the appeal of not just the money, but the fame, respect and glory of working in the most powerful medium in history is undeniable, but I think that it was a little too heady a wine, in that comics were really in danger of losing their souls in the process.

highlights.title: I hibernate in a couch lasagna beneath this microwaveable heated blanket
highlights.summary: Like Linus with his blankie, Bearaby’s Lounger is my constant companion when the weather gets brisk. My wife swears by weighted blankets to sleep – and now I understand why. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I n the early months of the pandemic, I enjoyed a brief flirtation with a 15lb weighted blanket from Amazon, but eventually abandoned it because it was impossible to launder and also sort of ugly. A few years later, I tried a different option – the sleep brand Bearaby’s flagship weighted blanket, an almost-but-not-quite-right solution that worked but eventually became cumbersome. In a frenzied afternoon spent deep cleaning, I set that one aside and eventually heaved it into the back of my sister’s Jeep for her.

Even though those two blankets didn’t stick, I still wanted something similar – just not ugly, large or hard to handle. Though I run hot and my apartment is often a furnace in the winter, my ideal leisure situation is enjoying the crisp air blowing in through a cracked window from the cozy and warm nest I’ve made on my sofa. Bearaby came to my rescue once more with the Lounger, a combination heated and weighted blanket that has been in my life for three years and is now my favorite thing in my apartment once winter sets in.

highlights.summary: Companies have spent the past several weeks trying to reassure investors that Muse and other AI agents pose more of an opportunity than a threat.
body: Meta’s Muse was among the hottest topics on corporate earnings calls in recent weeks. Meta has claimed that the agentic AI tool, which lets users automate various online tasks, is becoming a major force in shopping, with millions of people using it to make purchases of more than $200 on average.

Wall Street fears that proactive shopping assistants like Muse will erode brand loyalty, ignite price wars, and squeeze corporate profits. Yet on the earnings calls and in conversations with WIRED, executives across roughly 50 companies—spanning travel, internet providers, food, and self-storage—shrugged off immediate disruption. In fact, many insisted they would mostly benefit from any real widespread adoption of agents.

Food delivery app DoorDash described the number of orders from Muse and other agents as in the “hundreds.” T-Mobile remarked, “We haven’t seen anything of significance” from agents. Hotel chain Hilton was more direct, calling bookings from them “insignificant.” The banking provider Ally Financial characterized activity as “quite low,” while eBay termed it “very, very small.”
points: Companies have spent the past several weeks trying to reassure investors that Muse and other AI agents pose more of an opportunity than a threat.

highlights.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
highlights.summary: A biotech startup let an agent choose a gene therapy and successfully inject the treatment, offering a startling glimpse of the future of research labs.
body: If you give an AI agent a robotic arm, an injector, and a live mouse, it might just perform brain surgery.

Biotech founder Gabriel Ocana Santero recently did that using an agent to successfully carry out a brain injection procedure on a living mouse. Though it required some extra steps, it offers a glimpse into how AI could eventually become an active participant in laboratory research.

Santero posted about the experiment on social media and tells WIRED he was interested in exploring what happens when AI agents are given direct access to lab equipment, rather than simply being asked to design experiments or analyze results.

“We’ve realized that we need to connect these agents to a lab to get the maximum value from them,” he says. Santero is the CEO and cofounder of Exin Therapeutics, a San Francisco–based startup using AI to analyze brain activity to develop drugs for epilepsy and neurodegenerative diseases.

body: “I wanted to tell a story about a kind of love that is rarely at the center of films, yet it is so beautiful: the love between a brother and a sister,” Manchevski tells Variety. “It can be fierce, complicated, sometimes painful, but also unconditional like no other type of love.”

The director also took inspiration from traditional Macedonian songs about sisterly love, which he calls poignant and at times shocking. Of Malina and Viktor, he says: “They are far from ideal people. But they are deserving of understanding and affection. I am interested in people as they are, with their contradictions, not as examples of how people should behave. Idealized characters make for bad movies.”

The siblings break the law and sometimes make terrible mistakes, but Manchevski says he had no wish to turn them into objects of pity. He sees the pair’s refusal to think of themselves as victims as a way of reclaiming their own story.

highlights.title: The reason most electrical plug prongs have holes in them
highlights.summary: If you've ever looked at the end of a plug, you've probably wondered why some have holes, and some don't - and no, it's not actually a big conspiracy theory.
body: Of all the things in the world to sit back and contemplate, holes in electrical plug prongs are one of those great mysteries. It's right up there with the hollow moon theory and underground military bases in Antarctica. Not really. The truth is, while these enigmatic holes once served an everyday purpose (more on that below), they are mainly useful in the manufacturing process today. They help manufacturers position the metal blades during manufacturing, but they aren't openings for electrical current or portals to another dimension.

Basically, a worker passes an alignment rod through the holes to hold the blades in position before plastic is molded around the assembly. The holes also serve as lockout tags, a necessary safety mechanism. A once sensible purpose in the home is now a holding, positioning and locking convenience for manufacturers. It's a simple way to keep components correctly aligned during production. That goes for ordinary plugs on a vacuum cleaner to smart plugs for smart home integration (just don't plug a power strip into your smart plug ).
points: If you've ever looked at the end of a plug, you've probably wondered why some have holes, and some don't - and no, it's not actually a big conspiracy theory.
